records.section_heading: A Comparative Phylogenetic Investigation of Tridacninae: a Mitochondrial vs Nuclear Analysis
records.question: According to the section, are the mitochondrial and nuclear phylogenies congruent?
records.ground_truth_answer: No — the mitochondrial phylogeny is congruent with previous studies (Fauvelot et al 2020 and Tan et al 2021), while preliminary nuclear phylogenies built with 'Seanome' are incongruent with existing mitochondrial trees.
ground_truth_chunks: Our study's resulting mitochondrial phylogeny is congruent with the tree constructed in Fauvelot et al 2020 and Tan et al 2021.
Using the program 'Seanome', we built preliminary nuclear phylogenies which are incongruent with existing mitochondrial trees*.*

records.section_heading: First Record of Tridacna Noae in American Sāmoa
records.question: What methods did the authors use to identify Tridacna noae in the Samoan archipelago?
records.ground_truth_answer: They used morphologic characteristics and ez-RAD genetic techniques to identify Tridacna noae.
ground_truth_chunks: The most recent study of the status of giant clams in the Samoan Archipelago [was published ov](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/366840417)er 20 years ago, without molecular corroboration of visual identifications.

Using morphologic characteristics and ez-RAD genetic techniques, we identified the existence of *Tridacna noae* in the Samoan archipelago, presenting the first observation and a resulting range expansion.
